analysis.subject: biology
analysis.pageCoverage: The page introduces population genetics and descriptive statistics, defines biological and human populations, and explains why race and ethnicity are limited descriptors for estimating allele frequencies.

overview.headline: Overview of population genetics definitions and human population classification concepts

keyPoints.point: Population genetics examines distribution and change in allele frequencies under evolutionary forces
keyPoints.quote: Population genetics is the study of the distribution of and change in allele frequencies under the influence of the four evolutionary forces

keyPoints.point: Descriptive statistics summarize collection of population data in clear concise manner
keyPoints.quote: Descriptive statistics are used to summarize a collection of population data in a clear and concise manner.

keyPoints.point: In biology population denotes group whose members breed primarily or solely among themselves
keyPoints.quote: In biology, a population generally denotes a group whose members breed primarily or solely among themselves.

keyPoints.point: Research demonstrated racial classifications are inadequate descriptors of genetic variation distribution
keyPoints.quote: Research has demonstrated that racial classifications are inadequate descriptors of the distribution of genetic variation in the human species.

keyTerms.gloss: field that studies distribution and change of allele frequencies in populations
keyTerms.quote: Population genetics is the study of the distribution of and change in allele frequencies

keyTerms.gloss: distribution measure showing how often different alleles occur in a population
keyTerms.quote: Population genetics is the study of the distribution of and change in allele frequencies

keyTerms.gloss: pressures including natural selection drift mutation and migration that shape evolutionary forces
keyTerms.quote: the four evolutionary forces: natural selection, genetic drift, mutation, and migration.

keyTerms.gloss: methods used to summarize population data in a clear and concise manner
keyTerms.quote: Descriptive statistics are used to summarize a collection of population data in a clear and concise manner.

keyTerms.gloss: group whose members breed primarily or solely among themselves due to isolation
keyTerms.quote: In biology, a population generally denotes a group whose members breed primarily or solely among themselves.
